We will be holding our Annual Open Evening on Wednesday 30th September 2026. This is a wonderful opportunity to see the school, talk to members of staff and students, take part in activities and hear from our Headteacher. Please hold this date in your diary.
The evening runs from 5:30pm-8pm with Headteacher talks at 6pm and 7pm. No bookings necessary. Parking will be available through the North Drive Gates on Mereland Road, next to Willowcroft School.

Resources for Rising Year 7 Families
Admissions
The Governors of St Birinus School follow the Oxfordshire County Council schemes for processing applications to start Year 7 for the first time and in-year transfers during the school year.
To reserve a place for your son at St Birinus School, it is important to follow these procedures:
If your son is in Year 6, you will need to apply for secondary school transfer via your Council. If you live in Oxfordshire visit the Council website www.oxfordshire.gov.uk/secondaryadmissions for the link to the Parent Portal (School Places – Admissions) or to download the paper form (CAF Secondary) and read the information online (Moving On booklet). You can apply online or on paper. You do not need to do both. Contact the Council (see details below) if you need them to send you a paper form by email or post.
If you live in England but outside Oxfordshire, visit your local Council website for more information about how to apply.
If your son has already started in Secondary School and would like to transfer to St Birinus, you will need to apply via Oxfordshire County Council by visiting this website: https://www.oxfordshire.gov.uk/residents/schools/apply-school-place/year-transfers
Oxfordshire County Council School Admissions Team Contact Details
School Admissions Team, Oxfordshire County Council County Hall, New Road, Oxford, OX1 1ND
Email; admissions.schools@oxfordshire.gov.uk Web: www.oxfordshire.gov.uk/admissions
Y6 Primary Visits
Throughout September, we visit the Year 6 boys who attend primary schools within the Didcot Area Partnership. A senior member of staff, and current SBS students, deliver a presentation to the pupils and their parents, giving them information about our school and an idea of what life at St Birinus School is like.
For any families with boys attending primary schools outside the Didcot Area Partnership, we will be holding a presentation evening in September, details will follow.
Key Dates for Rising Year 7s each year
Our Year 7 Pupil Admission Number (PAN) is 240 for September 2026 entry
Applications open: early September each year
Closing date for applications: national closing date (31st October each year)
School offers sent out by the Council (on behalf of the school): national Offer Day (1 March each year or next working day). Emails are sent for those who apply online. Letters are sent (by second-class post) for those who apply on paper.
If you miss the National Closing Date, you can still apply online or on paper. Visit the Council website (see above).
Everyone who applies online by National Closing Date (31 October each year) will receive an email on National Offer Day (1 March each year or next working day) with details of the school offer for their child. The email may be the only formal notification sent. A letter will be sent (by second-class post) where an application was not online or where the first preference school was not offered or where the Council needs to send additional information.
Those who apply online will be able to respond online to accept or decline the place or change preferences or join waiting lists for schools where a place was not offered. Acceptance forms will be sent by post to those who did not apply online.
Welcome letter for September intake for Year 7 sent from St Birinus School during March each year (after National Offer Day).
We hold an Open Evening and series of Open Mornings every year in September/October to which all prospective families are welcome to attend. We also hold an evening, with www.didcotgirls.oxon.sch.uk/, for potential applicants into our mixed sixth form in November. Information about all of these events is clearly signed on our website well in advance of the events themselves.
To view our admissions arrangements please view the relevant documents below.
Click here to view the appeals procedure:
https://www.oxfordshire.gov.uk/residents/schools/starting-school/school-appeals

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Chair of Governors - St Birinus School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Chair of Governors
At St Birinus School, we have the very highest expectations for both our staff and students. There is a strong ethos which consistently runs through the school, supporting the core values of Inspiring Excellence through Care, Courtesy and Commitment.
The last Ofsted inspection in February 2020, adjudged the school to be a “Good” school, however, we are striving every day to better and deliver the highest standards of teaching and learning. Single sex education works. SBS boys achieve very well year in year out and many go on to study at Russell Group universities. Our vision is to equip the boys with the skills, knowledge and character to grab any opportunity and achieve their full potential and that is what we are focused on every day.
However, the focus is not simply on the academic. St Birinus is among the best schools in Oxfordshire in terms of offering a wide range of sports and extra-curricular activities, from football to archery, weightlifting to Warhammer. There is also a strong ethos in the arts, with a large number of boys engaged in Music, Dance and Drama.
Located a stone’s throw from Harwell’s Science campus, St Birinus is able to network and work closely with surrounding employers and businesses to help prepare the boys for their next steps into the world of work, supported by a thriving Careers and Leadership programme.
Although we are an all boys’ school, there is strong female influence running through the school from the Leadership Team down. As part of the Ridgeway Education Trust, St Birinus is part of a joint Sixth Form with Didcot Girls’ School which also affords the community joint events such as public speaking, dance shows, theatre productions and concerts for all our musicians.
Whilst St Birinus has strong traditions, we are a modern and forward thinking school. We are proud of our students and of our staff. If you want to find out more, contact our Headteacher, William Manning and visit the school (when possible) to see us in action.
Conor Byrne Chair of Governors

Reporting Absences
If your child is unable to attend school for any reason, please could parents/carers email attendance@st-birinus.oxon.sch.uk or call the Attendance Team on 01235 814444, Option 1 by 9:00am and leave a message. Please make sure you state:
Please speak clearly and spell any unusual names.
When your child returns to school please provide school with a note.
Students should attend school every day unless they are ill or have permission to be away. Dental and medical appointments should be made outside school hours where possible. If your child has an unavoidable appointment such as a hospital appointment, please inform the school in writing in advance of the appointment. We may require a copy of the appointment letter if this is a frequent occurrence. We will often contact home by text, phone or letter if you are absent and no reason has been provided. St Birinus is trying hard to work together with parents, carers and students to maintain and reward good attendance. pageCache.text:
Senior Leadership Team
Mr William Manning Headteacher wmanning@st-birinus.oxon.sch.uk
William Manning graduated from Kings' College London with a degree in French and Latin in 1994 and left university to pursue arabic studies in Egypt and then work in industry before completing a PGCE with Oxford University in 1999. William worked as a teacher of languages and a Head of Year at the Marlborough School, Woodstock and then subsequently as a Head of Year and Assistant Headteacher with pastoral responsibilities at Tanglin Trust School, Singapore.
Mr Graeme Irwin Deputy Headteacher - Raising Standards Leader girwin@st-birinus.oxon.sch.uk
Graeme Irwin graduated from Swansea University with a degree in Geography. After spending a year volunteering for a campus-based charity, Graeme returned to his studies in order to complete his PGCE in Geography Teaching. Starting his teaching career at Didcot Girls’ School, Graeme experienced a range of roles, including Head of Year & Assistant Headteacher, Head of Key Stage 3 before taking up a post in Hampshire as Deputy Headteacher of a rural Secondary School for three years.
Ms Julia Hopkins Deputy Headteacher - Curriculum Teaching & Learning RET Recruitment & Retention Lead jhopkins@st-birinus.oxon.sch.uk
Julia Hopkins graduated from the University of Gloucestershire with a degree in English Literature and Studies in Modern Writing in 2001. She then spent two years working as part of the occupational therapy team at a dual diagnosis unit for adults with learning difficulties and mental health illnesses at Oxfordshire NHS Learning Disability Trust. Following this Julia qualified as a teacher in 2004 and began teaching English at St Birinus in September of the same year. Prior to being appointed as Assistant Head Teacher, Julia held a range of posts across the school, including Head of English, Head of Year and Literacy Co-ordinator.
As Deputy Headteacher, Julia is responsible for ensuring consistently high quality teaching and learning at St Birinus and supporting its delivery through a programme of carefully designed CPD tailored to deliver the best for the students.
Mr James Cross Director of Sixth Form jcross@didcotsixthform.co.uk
James Cross graduated from the University of Oxford with a degree in English Literature and Language, before completing a PGCE at the University of Keele and teaching in the West Midlands. He returned to Oxfordshire in 2014 to work at Didcot Girls’ School, where has held a variety of roles, most recently as Head of English and Associate Senior Leader. He has also worked across a number of schools as a Specialist Leader of Education, supporting English departments with curriculum development and raising standards.
James is responsible for the Didcot Sixth Form, working across both St Birinus School and Didcot Girls' School. He lives in Didcot, though hails originally from the North, and enjoys anything that takes him to more mountainous terrain.
Mrs Sally Thom Assistant Headteacher - Learning and Culture Designated Safeguarding Lead sthom@st-birinus.oxon.sch.uk
Sally graduated from the University of Sheffield with a degree in Biochemistry and completed her PGCE at the University of Oxford. She began her teaching career at a school in central Oxford, holding various roles within the Science department and contributing to whole-school Teaching & Learning. Joining St Birinus School in 2020 as Head of Science, she now serves as an Assistant Headteacher, contributing to the Pastoral and Curriculum Leadership groups, focusing on supporting students and their academic success in addition to being the Designated Safeguarding Lead.
Mrs Rachel Lister Assistant Headteacher - Inclusion rlister@st-birinus.oxon.sch.uk
Rachel studied for her PGCE at the University of Bath following her French and Spanish Joint Honors degree. Having lived and worked in various Francophone and Hispanic countries, she spent many years as a French and Spanish teacher in inner-city schools in London, during which time she studied for her Masters in Education. She then became a MFL Consultant for a multi-academy trust leading on Spanish across 46 schools spanning the capital. This was a highly rewarding and varied role, however Rachel missed the sense of belonging she had had from working in one sole school, so made the sideways move into in-school Leadership and became the Raising Standards Lead at a mixed secondary school in Berkshire for three years. She started at St Birinus in January 2024 as Assistant Headteacher leading on Inclusion and thoroughly loves the sense of community and is committed to serving the students and staff at SBS.
Mr P Randall Assistant Headteacher prandall@st-birinus.oxon.sch.uk
​Mr J Wright Associate Senior Leader - Attendance and Data jwright@st-birinus.oxon.sch.uk

Careers Advice
Claire Tuckwell is the Acting Careers Lead for SBS. She can be contacted via: ctuckwell@ridgewayeducation.com
Claire is also our Careers Adviser. Claire provides impartial careers information, advice and guidance. She works predominantly with Year 11s helping them secure positive destinations for after their GCSEs, however any pupil or parent is welcome to contact Claire to ask any Careers related question and/or to arrange a Careers Advice Session. Claire has an office in the Main block, RAL Office on a Tuesday (students welcome to drop in during break/lunch) and in the Tech block (Governance office) on a Wednesday (students welcome by appointment).
The RET also employs a Work Experience Coordinator, Elianne Edgington to support those programmes that run in Years 9 and 10. Elianne can be contacted via: eedgington@ridgewayeducation.com. Please visit the Work Experience page here.
Careers Notices are emailed out fortnightly to all parents and students, promoting the latest careers events and opportunities, including webinars, podcasts, open days and work experience opportunities in a wide range of sectors. These can be accessed within the Careers Notices page. Careers Notices
The SBS Careers Provision focuses on fulfilling the following Learning Outcomes:
Pupils have ambitious career goals and the skills, knowledge and insight to achieve them
Pupils gain a broad knowledge and awareness of a wide range of careers and how their school subjects are relevant to them
Pupils feel informed and secure, making decisions on the next steps in their careers journey including transition points
Creating positive attitudes towards their careers journey including transition points
Developing pupils’ key employability skills: Communication, problem solving, time management, teamwork, leadership and organisation
Pupils can expect to participate in and experience a wide range of enriching and informative careers related experiences during their time at SBS. Those experiences are summed up in our Careers Journey infographic:

pageCache.text:
Starting your Teaching Career at SBS
St Birinus is a great school in which to begin and develop your career in teaching. We are committed to making staff feel valued and to provide support for developing their skills so that they can realise their full potential.
"staff are committed to improving their practice and report that they are well supported by both middle and senior leaders"
We believe that the most important thing that happens in school is good teaching in every classroom, every day. In order to ensure this for each child we invest in the professional development for all staff to enable this to happen. We provide opportunities to collaborate in professional contexts to improve teaching and learning practice and provide a CPD programme aimed at developing the areas that are most wanted by staff. We embrace a growth mindset approach to education for both staff and students and look to find the right staff to work in this exciting environment where you will be encouraged and supported to progress in your career aspirations.

Careers Information for Staff
St Birinus School are developing a network of department based ‘Careers Champions’.
The group will meet approximately 3 times a year and will aim to:
Planned actions include: department-based careers conferences, career displays in departments, and subject-specific careers information threaded through the curriculum. Your Head of Department or Claire Tuckwell, as Acting Careers Lead, will be able to tell you who your own department Careers Champion is in due course. If you are interested in becoming a Careers Champion or initiating a careers related event within your subject, please do speak to Claire.
For careers resources for your own use as a teacher and to advise or guide students, we recommend using Unifrog. For further advice and guidance, please get in touch with Claire Tuckwell ctuckwell@ridgewayeducation.com.
Claire Tuckwell is also our RET Careers Adviser. Claire works at Didcot Girls’ School on Mondays and Thursdays and St Birinus School on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Claire’s office is in the Maths block, opposite M1 (Tuesday) and in the Tech block, Governance office on (Wednesday). Claire provides impartial careers information, advice and guidance.
For Work Experience and Takeover Challenge queries, please contact Elianne Edgington by emailing eedgington@ridgewayeducation.com
Our RET Careers Lead is Stuart George who can be contacted by emailing sgeorge@ridgewayeducation.com
